Witty editorial advertising still life, 4:5 vertical frame, for an Indian demi-fine jewellery brand. On a pale ivory lime-plaster surface, a small heap of ripe glossy jamun fruit, deep purple-black with a dusty bloom, sits at the upper right, one jamun bitten open to show its violet flesh, a purple juice stain on the plaster. The pair of gold huggie hoops lies in the lower middle, their row of soft AMETHYST-LILAC baguette stones (not red: the stones in IMAGE 1 are amethyst-lilac) answering the fruit's violet.

THE PRODUCT: IMAGE 1 is our approved product photograph and the authority on this exact piece: its construction, size, metal colour and stone colour; ignore its plaster cube, background and light. IMAGE 2 is the supplier photograph of the same piece, for construction detail only; ignore everything else in it. Preserve the piece exactly: do not redesign, restyle, resize or add anything. CONSTRUCTION LOCK: HUGGIE HOOP earrings in warm gold, about 18mm across, hinged with a snap closure: the lower front half of each hoop is set with a single row of ruby-red BAGUETTE stones standing crosswise side by side in gold claws; the upper half is plain polished gold. One row of crosswise red baguettes on the lower half only; ruby red, never pink; gold metal.

SCALE TEST: Each huggie is about 18mm across; each jamun is about 20mm long, close to one hoop; each baguette is 4mm. The jewellery keeps its true small size against the referent; it dominates by light and isolation, never by being enlarged.

COPY SPACE: The upper left third of the frame is calm, empty ivory plaster, softly lit, for a headline.

LIGHT: soft large window light from the upper left, one soft natural shadow, plus ONE small hard specular kicker from the right, so the metal shows a crisp bright edge and a dark rolled edge on every curve and every stone carries internal sparkle and one pure-white catchlight, never flat colour. Honest macro optics: the jewellery is needle-sharp and the scene falls softly out of focus behind it. Real texture everywhere: grain, fibre, dust, believable imperfection, nothing plastic. 

ABSENCE LIST: No text, no letters, no logo, no watermark, no price tag anywhere in frame. No hands, no people. No second piece of jewellery. No border, no vignette: the photograph fills the frame edge to edge.

Three small handmade paper akash kandil lanterns, star-shaped, one aqua, one soft pink, one pale butter yellow, glow softly from within at the upper right, slightly out of focus; below them on a pale ivory lime-plaster floor the bracelet lies open in a gentle curve, each pastel stone carrying the glow of the lantern of its own colour. Preserve the bracelet from reference 1 exactly, with its stones built exactly as in reference 2: a continuous line of square cushion-cut stones about 5mm each in the repeating order aqua blue, soft pink, pale yellow, every stone framed by its own fine pave halo of tiny clear stones, linked in rhodium silver tone with a fold-over clasp. LIGHT: the lanterns' soft coloured glow, a soft warm fill from the left, one small hard kicker giving the silver a crisp edge and every stone a white catchlight.
